items.text: Bobby Lewis's "Tossin' and Turnin'" spent seven weeks at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in July and August 1961, the year's longest-running number one.
items.question: Where were you that summer when "Tossin' and Turnin'" was number one, and who were you with?
source_quote: The Billboard Hot 100 is a chart published since August 1958 by Billboard magazine which ranks the best-performing singles in the United States. In 1961, it was compiled based on a combination of sales and airplay data sourced from surveys of retail outlets and playlists submitted by radio stations respectively. During the year, 22 different singles spent time at number one.
The year's longest-running number one was "Tossin' and Turnin'" by Bobby Lewis, which spent seven weeks in the top spot in July and August.

items.text: Roger Maris of the New York Yankees hit his 61st home run on October 1, 1961, in the last game of the season, beating the record held by Babe Ruth.
items.question: Who in your family followed Roger Maris's chase of Babe Ruth's record, and where were you when you heard he hit number 61?
items.source_quote: October 1 – Baseball player Roger Maris of the New York Yankees hits his 61st home run in the last game of the season, against the Boston Red Sox, beating the 34-year-old record held by Babe Ruth.
